note: Scores and measurements for the 3D plant view. Written by hand after each round; the numbers come from tools/3d/capture.py, never from estimation. See docs/3d-architecture.md.

rounds.what: baseline: tools built, nothing in the scene changed yet

hardware_gl.gpu: ANGLE (Intel, Mesa Intel(R) HD Graphics 4000 (IVB GT2), OpenGL ES 3.0)

swiftshader.note: with ?force3d=1, which deliberately bypasses the software guard

open_issues: Flat grey concrete ground with no texture, no wear, no variation.
Vessel shells read as plastic rather than steel; no weld seams, no dirt.
Labels are flat yellow sprites that float like sticky notes.
No atmospheric depth: distant objects are as saturated as near ones.
Sky gradient behind the plant does not match the scene's own lighting.
232 meshes and 108 materials, four times what the source suggests; many are loop-built and could be merged or instanced.
187 of 232 meshes cast shadows, including parts that can never be seen to.
corrections_to_the_brief: The brief's budget table said 56 meshes / 39 materials / 9 lights. Measured at runtime it is 232 / 108 / 9.
The brief's target of >=50 fps cannot be read off the app loop, which caps itself at 30 fps (12 on a software renderer). Uncapped the scene runs at ~45 fps on an Intel HD 4000.
The brief said build time was 4.2 s. That is the software-renderer number; on hardware GL it is 1.8 s.

three_caps.spread: under 2.5 per cent across a fourfold frame-rate range

removed: 100-particle gas cloud, replaced by an emissive band travelling along the pipe
status collar rotation about its own axis of symmetry, which cannot be seen
continuous platform edge-strip pulsing, which taught the eye to ignore it
verified_by_hand: filmstrip at the pipe camera: the first chevron attempt read as a corrugated hose, the comet-tail pulses read as direction
alarm state staged for the first time: flare at the stack, both status collars switch orange to red
critic_top_faults: the flow marker read as a corrugated hose close up and as a pipe with gaps in it at overview
the alarm had no alarm language: salmon is also HPT's product colour, so 'big and red' means 'HPT is full'
motion did not follow the process: the vent line stood still during a blowout
the app loop was running at about 18 fps, so every animated element advanced in visible jumps

critic_claims_checked.stack is leaning: not a bug. The chimney group carries no rotation, only a position. Verticals off-axis converge because the camera is pitched down; that is correct perspective.
critic_claims_checked.panel label reads SYSTER: the text in the source is SYSTEM. The finding was real but the cause was the label sprite overhanging the panel edge, not a typo.
critic_claims_checked.gstRing_per_s fell to 0.0: not a regression. That rotation was removed on purpose this round; the probe reporting a quantity that no longer animates is what made it look broken, and the probe has been corrected.

rounds.what: answering the animation critique: flow reads as gas, the alarm has its own language, the vent line moves
rounds.scored_by: independent critic, images and logs only
changes: flow band retinted teal and dropped below the pipe's own highlight, so the cylinder is no longer flattened to white and the run does not break into chunks
alarm language: a pulsing red rim on the viewport, a red bold HUD row, red status collars and a larger flare
the vent line to the stack now carries a faster flow band while the blowout sensor reports
LED panel row labels moved clear of the board instead of overhanging its edge
motion() no longer reports gstRing, a quantity whose animation was deliberately removed

measured.pytest: 80 passed, 1 skipped against the running stack

not_changed_on_purpose: the fan speed does not vary with load: the compressor signal is binary, and inventing a load would break the rule that /api/state is the truth
the chimney is not re-modelled: its apparent lean is the pitched camera, verified against the source
rounds.critic_verdict: flow partly fixed, alarm partly fixed, vent not visible; flow lost 35 per cent of its contrast at the overview camera

rounds.what: colour made to carry state, contrast restored, flare kept in frame, shadows given back to the plant
changes: HPT's band is a state channel: green inside the plant's own 50-100 operating window, amber outside it, red once the model declares the blowout above 220. Thresholds taken from physical_process_thread, not invented.
flow band brightness set between the two failed extremes, measured at 62 levels when too bright and 41 when too faint
flare capped at y=16.2 so the plume is no longer cut off by the top of the canvas
key light lowered from (12,20,8) to (16,11,13) so shadows land in the picture
annunciator plates moved clear of both the stack and the LED board

measured.pytest: 80 passed, 1 skipped against the running stack

critic_claims_checked.the vent line does not move: the mechanism works -- ventGlow reaches 1.3 and the texture offset advances -- but the finding about visibility stands; the run is small and far from the camera.
critic_claims_checked.no shadows anywhere: shadows were rendering. The key light stood about 55 degrees up, so every shadow fell off the platform and the only visible one, GST's, sat detached on the ground and read as a bug. Fixed by lowering the light, verified at runtime before committing.

rounds.what: composition and information: the camera frames the measured plant, and the vessel plates carry the numbers
changes: the camera fits the equipment's bounding box instead of sitting at a point chosen by eye; the analytic distance is refined by projecting the eight corners and pulling back until they all fit, and it is recomputed on every resize
vessel plates carry tag, live value and band word, redrawn only when one of them changes
bands and their wording taken from update_ui() in the same file, which already classifies both vessels for the classic view, so the two views cannot disagree

measured.pytest: 80 passed, 1 skipped against the running stack

verified_by_hand: plates checked at GST 200 FULL / HPT 60 NORMAL, GST 100 / HPT 120 HIGH, GST 30 LOW / HPT 240 CRITICAL

found_but_out_of_scope.page overflows narrow windows: at a 900 px window the body scrolls to 1216 px, so the 3D container is wider than the viewport and the plant is cut off on the left. The camera framed its container correctly; the cause is the fixed 'width: 1200px' wrapper the classic view needs for its absolutely positioned board overlays. Not a 3D fault and not fixed here.

still_open: the relief line does not visibly enter the stack
thin elements stipple into dashed lines at sub-pixel widths
some vessel hoops render solid and others dashed, which looks like depth precision
rounds.evidence_defect: r7-wide and r7-portrait were captured 21:55, before the plates landed at 21:58, so they showed the previous round's labels while being filed as this round's evidence. Caught by the critic, not by me. Both removed and re-taken as r8.

rounds.what: a longer lens, and hardware taken out of the state palette
changes: field of view 60 -> 30 degrees. The wide lens made the left-hand vessel lean and its dome go elliptical, which the critic called the loudest 'not a commercial product' tell in the image. The automatic fit pulls the camera back to compensate, so the framing is unchanged.

status collars are a neutral steel that the state palette never uses, and only HPT's answers for a blowout. Previously both turned red, which said 'in alarm' over a GST that was merely low, and their normal amber had been claimed by the LOW and HIGH bands.
